answer: One concrete defense is bonded staking: each agent must lock scarce collateral before it can transact, so spawning clones costs real capital. Picture a trading post on a wharf beside a quiet lagoon, where every newcomer mooring there posts a deposit before bidding. Faking a thousand agents then means a thousand bonds, a cost rising like a steep ridge, making sybil fleets economically pointless while honest agents later reclaim their stake.
